processing.downmixRationale: first-order B-format (AmbiX/ACN: W, Y, Z, X) decoded to stereo as L = W + 0.7Y, R = W - 0.7Y; the mono sum is 2W, the omni capsule. Z and X unused - no height or depth to put them in.
processing.channelBalanceRationale: measured standing L/R difference, halved onto each channel: the cabin really is louder on one side, but a bed played for eight hours should not leave one ear hotter all night
processing.loudnorm: two-pass linear, I=-20.68 LUFS, TP=-1.0 dBTP, LRA=11
processing.loopStartRationale: start chosen so the 6s before the wrap and the 6s after it sit at the same level at P=251s; trimming from 0 put a fade-in against a settled tail

notes: Private first-class sleeper cabin, windows closed: railway clicks, rumble, occasional squeak. Downmixed from ambisonic B-format and levelled by tools/level-ftus.py. Checked before shipping: faster-whisper with VAD finds zero speech segments in either cabin variant, and the tonal events tools/scan-tonal-events.py reports are the railway squeaks themselves — this bed is metallic by nature, so the scanner's usual 'narrow and tonal means intruder' reading does not hold here. Seamless-looped to 251s (prime loopOffset) for native Howler looping: 6s fade-wrap of the post-loop tail over the head so the loop point is gapless. Encoded as Opus (128k) — see DECISIONS.md 'Ship scene audio as Opus, not MP3'.
recordedWith: ZOOM F6 + Rode NT-SF1 (first-order ambisonic mic) — from the master's BWF metadata, which is what confirms the W,Y,Z,X filename prefix is a real B-format layout and not a naming quirk
